items.title: How Evolution Shaped Our Moral Sense | Nathan Lents
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Why would evolution favor people who help others who may never repay them?*

Nathan Lents explores how human morality may have emerged from empathy, cooperation, and the evolutionary advantages of living in supportive groups. He argues that compassion need not depend on calculating personal rewards and explains why broadly generous instincts may have helped early human communities survive.

0:00 Morality Begins With Cognitive Empathy
1:48 Beyond Bookkeeping Reciprocity
2:55 Why Caring Groups Tend to Win
4:26 Group Selection and the Enforcement of Fairness
6:00 Keeping the Instinct Vague

*Nathan H. Lents* is an American scientist, author, and university professor. He has been on the faculty of John Jay College since 2006 and is currently the director of the Cell and Molecular Biology program and the former head of the honors program and the campus Macaulay Honors College program.

items.title: Can Synchronicity Be Studied Scientifically? | Jeffrey Mishlove
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:

Jeffrey Mishlove examines Carl Jung's theory of synchronicity and why spontaneous coincidences present unusual difficulties for parapsychological research. He considers possible connections to flow states, psychotherapy, fractal patterns, and mystical traditions while questioning how far scientific methods can reach.

*Jeffrey Mishlove* is a parapsychologist with a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and Host and Producer of the New Thinking Allowed YouTube channel. items.title: How to Test Whether Art Deepens Understanding | Christopher Brewer
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Can reading a novel make someone more compassionate, or does it only change how they feel?*

Christopher Brewer explores how researchers could investigate the relationship between art and understanding through carefully designed experiments. From the illustrations surrounding ancient manuscripts to the language people use to describe awe and the sublime, he explains why defining experiences precisely is essential before their effects can be tested.

items.author: Closer To Truth

items.title: The Case Against Three Arguments for God's Existence | Michael Tooley
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Does the universe need a first cause, or could causes extend backward forever?*

Michael Tooley challenges several traditional arguments for God's existence, questioning whether an infinite regress is logically impossible and whether biological complexity requires a designer. He also examines a limitation he sees in fine-tuning arguments: changing one physical constant at a time may yield different conclusions from varying many constants together.

0:00 Three Problems with Cosmological Arguments
1:04 The Possibility of Infinite Causal Regress
2:26 First Causes and Necessary Existence
4:20 Evolution and the Argument from Design
5:28 Fine-Tuning and Changing All the Constants

*Michael Tooley* is Emeritus Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at the University of Colorado Boulder. He received a Boulder Faculty Assembly Excellence in Research Award in 1998 for his book _Time, Tense, and Causation,_ and is the author of the new book _Causation: A Defense of a Non-Reductionist Approach_ (Oxford, 2026).

items.title: Why Bergson Says Time Cannot Be Divided into Moments | Victoria Trumbull
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if the time we measure is not the time we actually experience?*

Victoria Trumbull explains Henri Bergson's concept of duration, where the past, present, and future unfold continuously rather than as separate moments. She explores why the mind spatializes time for practical purposes and how different forms of duration may illuminate the relationship between consciousness and matter.

0:00 Bergson's Concept of Duration
3:00 Multiplicity Without Divisibility
5:53 Succession Without Separation
7:09 Why the Mind Spatializes Time
10:21 Memory and Matter as Different Durations
14:19 Duration Extends into the Material World
16:39 Bergson's Relevance to Modern Science

*Victoria Trumbull* is a philosopher, researcher, and writer whose work concerns the nature of the mind and the relationship between time, memory, and the soul. She received her DPhil from the University of Oxford and is the author of _On the Memory of the Soul: Augustine and Bergson’s Metaphysics._

items.title: God and Physics May Explain Different Kinds of Causes | Charles Harper
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*If physics explains how the universe began, does that leave any role for God?*

Charles Harper revisits Aristotle's four causes to question whether physical and divine explanations must compete. He explores how mathematics, matter, and mind complicate the search for an ultimate cause, while warning theologians against invoking God or ultimate mystery to prematurely close scientific questions.

*Charles L. Harper Jr.* is a philanthropic consultant, philosopher of science, and theologian who formerly served as Executive Director and Senior Vice President of the John Templeton Foundation. His work spans planetary science, cosmology, and the relationship between science and theology, with particular interests in the nature of time, quantum theory, and the foundations of physical reality.

items.title: Why More Consciousness Theories May Mean Progress | Robert Lawrence Kuhn | Àlex Gómez-Marín
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*In a first for Closer To Truth, the roles are reversed: Àlex Gómez-Marín interviews Robert Lawrence Kuhn, the creator and host of the series.*

*Why does studying consciousness produce more theories instead of fewer?*

Robert Lawrence Kuhn explains why the expanding landscape of consciousness theories may represent intellectual progress, how he immersed himself in competing perspectives, and why he ultimately included a deliberately brief and internally inconsistent account of his own views.

0:00 Consciousness as a Window into Ultimate Reality
4:28 More Knowledge, More Theories, Every Scale
7:33 Wearing Each Theory's Clothes
9:26 How Other Thinkers Reshaped the Landscape
12:10 Why Kuhn Reluctantly Disclosed His Own View

*Robert Lawrence Kuhn* is the creator, executive producer, writer, and host of Closer To Truth, which has featured more than 500 leading scientists, philosophers, and creative thinkers in more than 5,000 videos and more than 350 public television episodes on PBS stations. He holds a PhD in anatomy/neuroscience from the UCLA Brain Research Institute and an MBA from MIT's Sloan School of Management. He is the author or editor of more than 30 books, including _The Mystery of Existence: Why Is There Anything At All?_ (with John Leslie), and the author of the Landscape of Consciousness, a taxonomy of more than 500 theories of consciousness.

*Àlex Gómez-Marín* is a Spanish physicist turned neuroscientist. He holds a PhD in theoretical physics and a Masters in biophysics from the University of Barcelona. He was a research fellow at the EMBL-CRG Centre for Genomic Regulation and at the Champalimaud Centre for the Unknown in Lisbon. His research spans from the origins of the arrow of time in inert systems, to the neurobiology of action-perception in living organisms such as flies, worms, mice, and humans.

items.title: The Missing Concept That Could Unite Mind and Brain | Thomas Nagel
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if the mind and brain are necessarily connected, but we lack the concepts to understand how?*

Thomas Nagel revisits the history of mind-brain identity theory and Saul Kripke's influential challenge to it. He explains why imagining an experience from the inside differs from describing its neurological basis, and considers whether both perspectives might ultimately arise from something more fundamental.

0:00 From Behaviorism to Mind-Brain Identity Theory

19:44 The Legacy of Mind-Brain Identity Theory

*Thomas Nagel* is an American philosopher and Professor of Philosophy and Law at New York University. His work focuses on philosophy of mind, ethics, and political philosophy, and he is especially known for his influential critique of reductionist accounts of consciousness.

items.title: Has the Meaning of God's Name Changed Over Time? | Meghan Sullivan
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if an overlooked obstacle to knowing God is knowing whom we're talking about?*

Meghan Sullivan explores how religious knowledge depends on language passed down through generations. Drawing on Saul Kripke's philosophy of naming, she examines whether divine names can retain their original reference and why describing God simply as the creator of the universe may not resolve the problem.

0:00 Knowing God Through Religious Experience and Tradition
1:17 How Divine Names Can Change Their Reference
2:58 How Traditions Protect God's Name
5:00 The Skeptical Puzzle Outside Tradition
5:30 Why God Can't Just Be a Description

items.title: Behind the Scenes of Closer To Truth | Robert Lawrence Kuhn, Interviewed by Àlex Gómez-Marín
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*In a first for Closer To Truth, the roles are reversed: Àlex Gómez-Marín interviews Robert Lawrence Kuhn, the creator and host of the series.*

*What does it take to turn life's biggest questions into television?*

Robert Lawrence Kuhn explains why _Closer To Truth_ maintains high production values despite the commercial challenges, and how thousands of interview segments become carefully structured television episodes.

0:00 Why Closer To Truth Invests in Production Quality
1:52 From Raw Interviews to PBS Episodes
5:51 Building a Story From a Matrix of Interviews
7:49 The Physical Journey as a Metaphor
9:06 Looking Beyond 25 Years of Closer To Truth

*Robert Lawrence Kuhn* is the creator, executive producer, writer, and host of Closer To Truth, which has featured more than 500 leading scientists, philosophers, and creative thinkers in more than 5,000 videos and more than 350 public television episodes on PBS stations. He holds a PhD in anatomy/neuroscience from the UCLA Brain Research Institute and an MBA from MIT's Sloan School of Management. He is the author or editor of more than 30 books, including The Mystery of Existence: Why Is There Anything At All? (with John Leslie), and the author of the Landscape of Consciousness, a taxonomy of more than 500 theories of consciousness.

*Àlex Gómez-Marín* is a Spanish physicist turned neuroscientist. He holds a PhD in theoretical physics and a Masters in biophysics from the University of Barcelona. He was a research fellow at the EMBL-CRG Centre for Genomic Regulation and at the Champalimaud Centre for the Unknown in Lisbon. His research spans from the origins of the arrow of time in inert systems, to the neurobiology of action-perception in living organisms such as flies, worms, mice, and humans.
